gap: No single result ChatGPT got sets out the add-on limits across its CD picks: on both makers' pages I opened (Pioneer DEH-S4220BT and JVC KD-T920BTS), factory steering-wheel buttons need a separately sold adapter. The JVC is SiriusXM-ready but needs a tuner sold separately. The Pioneer's page lists no SiriusXM input, Alexa only through the Pioneer Smart Sync app, USB control only for iPhone 5s and newer, and FLAC/WAV only from USB, not from CD.
standout_why: Pioneer's DEH-S4220BT page (results 1-4) and JVC's KD-T920BTS page (result 5) each state their own model's limits, so the facts exist one model at a time in ChatGPT's results. My only new contribution is putting the models side by side. Abt (result 6) already states FLAC from a USB drive at up to 44.1 kHz/16-bit. World Wide Stereo's guide lists the Sony MEX-N5300BT but says nothing about SiriusXM, steering-wheel adapters or iPhone USB in the part I could read. The cited Crutchfield guide and the Crutchfield DEH-S4220BT Q&A both returned 403, so I could not check whether they already cover the adapter or SiriusXM points. That is why this is 1 and not 2.
decides: A shopper who wants SiriusXM should pick the JVC KD-T920BTS, the only model whose maker page I opened that says SiriusXM-ready, and budget for the tuner. A shopper who wants Alexa or hi-res files from USB should pick the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT. Either way, the shopper needs a steering-wheel adapter to keep the factory steering-wheel buttons.
